text: dsh-request-params 是供 DSH Web 客户端使用的模型请求参数插件，可按模型渠道或自定义网关，为发出的请求添加、替换或移除 JSON 字段与请求头。它在侧栏提供参数配置页，并通过包装全局 fetch 应用规则；页面可按主机、路径和模型匹配规则，预览变更、试运行并查看最近请求。内置 OpenRouter 供应商排序与回退、reasoning、sampling 等预设，也支持自定义参数、导入导出和暂停全部规则。适合需要调整模型网关请求格式或 OpenRouter 路由的人。插件自身不要求额外 API key；模型服务凭证仍由 DSH 渠道配置。

dsh-request-params configures JSON fields and headers on DSH model requests. Its Web page organizes rules by channel or gateway, matches hosts, paths, and models, and offers previews and request logs. Presets cover OpenRouter routing, reasoning, and sampling; custom rules support other gateways.

I need to add custom JSON fields to requests sent to an LLM gateway.
How can I choose and order OpenRouter providers for model calls?
dsh-request-params 的功能「OpenRouter 供应商路由」：在参数页选择供应商、排序并设定回退等条件，规则会匹配对应模型请求并写入 provider 路由字段。
dsh-request-params 的功能「自定义请求参数」：按主机、路径和模型配置请求规则，可合并或默认填入 JSON 字段、移除字段，并设置或移除普通请求头。
dsh-request-params 的功能「预览与试运行」：在页面选择模型后查看规则将添加的请求内容，也可对样例请求执行 dry run，便于保存前检查匹配结果。
dsh-request-params 的功能「请求记录」：查看经过拦截器的近期模型请求、应用的变更和响应状态，帮助判断规则是否匹配及网关如何回应。
dsh-request-params 的功能「按渠道管理规则」：读取 DSH 已配置的模型渠道及其地址，用户可为渠道建立参数规则，也能为其他主机指定匹配条件。
dsh-request-params 会读取 OpenRouter 公共目录及更新信息；插件说明称这些请求不携带规则、密钥或对话文本。请求记录保存在内存，失败响应最多留取前 2 KB。

dsh-request-params README · Request Parameters (dsh-request-params)：English | [中文](README.zh.md)

**Add your own parameters to every model request [dsh](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) sends.** OpenRouter provider routing, fallback models, reasoning effort, sampling extras, gateway headers, or any JSON field a gateway accepts. Pick one of the channels dsh already has, add parameters on a page instead of in code, see exactly what each request will carry before anything is sent, and see what the gateway answered afterwards.
dsh-request-params README · Request Parameters (dsh-request-params)：

dsh-request-params README · Why：dsh sends the fields its model adapters know about. Gateways such as [OpenRouter](https://openrouter.ai) take more: which providers to use and in what order, fallback models, a reasoning budget, a session ID for cache affinity. dsh does not send OpenRouter's `provider` routing preferences. Plugins exist for single slices of this (provider order and quantization, for example); this one is general. The same page handles any field or header for any gateway, with a ready form for OpenRouter's routing options, a live preview, and a log.

dsh-request-params README · Why：Each *parameter* belongs to a channel (or names its own hosts, models, and paths) and says what to add, replace, or remove in the body and headers. Parameters are applied to the request just before it leaves dsh; in the rules file each one is a *rule*.

dsh-request-params README · Highlights：- **Organized by channel.** The page lists the model channels dsh is set up with (the official DeepSeek channel and each one configured in `llm-pi-ai`) and the address each one sends to. Open a channel to see its parameters and add one in a click; it is matched to that channel for you. Parameters for any other address are under **Other addresses**.
- **Knows what each channel reads.** Each channel shows which request format it reads (OpenAI or Anthropic) and which extra fields (OpenRouter's `provider` and `reasoning`, vLLM's `chat_template_kwargs`, …), worked out from dsh's settings and its address. The kinds of parameter it reads come first; the rest wait under **Other kinds**. A gateway of your own that speaks OpenRouter's protocol gets provider routing once you tick **OpenRouter fields** for it.
- **See what will be sent.** **Added when sending** shows, as JSON, what the channel's parameters add to a request for the model you pick, including unsaved edits. Nothing is sent.
- **Pick providers, do not hand-write JSON.** **Provider routing** is one list: search providers (the ones that serve the previewed model come first, with price and uptim

dsh-request-params README · Install：```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-request-params
```

If you run dsh from source, use `pnpm dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-request-params`. Restart `dsh web` afterwards. A **Request Params** entry appears in the sidebar below **Plugins**.

To try a checkout, use `link:/path/to/dsh-request-params` instead of the name.

dsh-request-params README · Quick start: OpenRouter in two minutes：Pick an OpenRouter model in the composer.
2. Open **Request Params** and pick the **openrouter** channel. Click **Provider routing**, type a provider such as `deepseek` and press Enter, set **Other providers** to **Never** if no other provider may serve the request, and press **Save** (or Ctrl/⌘ + S). **Added when sending** shows the `provider` object; put the model you use in its **Model** box, and if a provider is flagged as not serving it, pick another provider or model.
3. Send a message. The channel's **Recent requests** shows what was added and the gateway's status.

dsh-request-params README · What you can add：| Kind | Adds | Typical use |
|---|---|---|
| **Provider routing** | `provider` (`order`, `only`, `ignore`, `allow_fallbacks`, `require_parameters`, `data_collection`, `zdr`, `quantizations`, `sort`, `max_price`, `preferred_min_throughput`, `preferred_max_latency`, `enforce_distillable_text`) and `models` | Choose providers and order, cap the price, require zero data retention, fall back to other models |
| **Reasoning effort** | `reasoning` (`effort`, `max_tokens`, `exclude`) | Turn thinking up or down, or keep it out of the reply |
| **Sampling extras** | `top_k`, `min_p`, `top_a`, `repetition_penalty` | Sampling fields the standard API does not have |
| **Session stickiness** | `session_id` in the body and the `x-session-id` header | Keep one conversation on one provider so caches hit |
| **App attribution** | `HTTP-Referer` and `X-OpenRouter-Title` headers | Credit your traffic to your app on OpenRouter (dsh does not send these) |
| **Remove fields** | removes fields such as `store` | A gateway that rejects a field dsh sends |
| **Custom fields and headers** | anything: JSON fields, headers, removals | Any other gateway |

dsh-request-params README · What you can add：Which kinds a channel offers first follows what it reads (see **What a channel reads** below). An OpenRouter channel offers every kind; a channel that reads the OpenAI format offers sampling extras, custom fields, session stickiness, and remove fields; an Anthropic channel offers the last three. The examples for other gateways (turn thinking off on a self-hosted vLLM with `chat_template_kwargs`, Helicone headers, Cloudflare AI Gateway cache headers, and an OpenAI `prompt_cache_key`) come first on a channel that is that gateway. Everything else is under **Other kinds**, each marked with what it needs, and can still be added. Each example is an ordinary custom parameter you can edit. **Other addresses** offers everything.

dsh-request-params README · What a channel reads：Under its address, each channel shows its protocol: the request format it reads and the extra fields it reads on top.

dsh-request-params README · What a channel reads：- **Worked out for you**: the format comes from the channel's `api` setting in `llm-pi-ai` (`openai-completions`, `anthropic-messages`, …), from the official DeepSeek channels (Anthropic), from the hosted service, or from the paths of the requests seen. Hosted services are recognized by their address: openrouter.ai (OpenRouter fields), helicone.ai, gateway.ai.cloudflare.com, and api.openai.com.
- **Yours to correct**: **Change** sets the format and ticks the fields the endpoint reads. The common case is a gateway of your own that speaks OpenRouter's protocol: tick **OpenRouter fields**, and provider routing, reasoning effort, and app attribution come first on that channel. The setting is saved with the parameters under the endpoint's host and base path; **Use what was detected** removes it.
- **What it changes**: only which kinds come first and how sure the catalog hints are. Requests are sent as the parameters say, whatever the protocol.
- **Catalog hints**: the provider list and whether a provider serves a model come from the public OpenRouter catalog. For a parameter that goes to openrouter.ai, a provider list none of which serves

dsh-request-params README · Writing your own parameter：- **Body fields**: a JSON object merged into the body. Objects merge with what is there; anything else is replaced.
- **Headers**: added to the request; a header of the same name is replaced.
- Under **More**: **Defaults** (like body fields, but a field the request already has is left alone), **Remove fields** (dotted paths such as `store` or `stream_options.include_usage`; removal happens first, then fields are set), **Remove headers**, and **Allow changing core fields**.

dsh-request-params README · Writing your own parameter：Every parameter has a scope. On a channel, **All models** limits it to some of the channel's models (`deepseek/*`, `*-chat`), and **Edit hosts and paths** in its menu shows the address it matches. Under **Other addresses** a parameter names its own *hosts* (`openrouter.ai`, `*.example.com`, `127.0.0.1:8130`), optional *models*, and optional *paths* (prefix). Without a path, it reaches model endpoints only (`…/chat/completions`, `…/messages`, `…/responses`, `…:generateContent`); name a path to reach another endpoint.

dsh-request-params README · Writing your own parameter：When several parameters apply to one request they run from top to bottom, and a later one sees the result of the earlier ones. Values may use `{{model}}` (the request's model), `{{session}}` (the dsh session ID; for channels where dsh sends none, a stable key derived from the conversation), and `{{env:NAME}}` (an environment variable; if it is not set the field is skipped and the log says so).
dsh-request-params README · Writing your own parameter：

dsh-request-params README · Safety and privacy：- `messages`, `system`, `tools`, `tool_choice`, `input`, `instructions`, `prompt`, `contents`, `stream`, and `model` cannot be set or removed unless a custom parameter explicitly allows it.
- `Authorization`, `x-api-key`, `api-key`, `x-goog-api-key`, `Cookie`, `Host`, and the headers that frame the request (`Content-Length`, `Content-Type`, …) can never be changed.
- A parameter with a problem is not applied, and the page shows what is wrong. If applying parameters fails while a request is being sent, the request goes out unchanged and the log says so.
- Parameters are stored on your machine in `<profile>/.dsh-request-params/config.json`. Nothing is sent anywhere because of them.
- The request log lives in memory only (the last 50 requests; cleared on restart). It holds the model, the address, and the changes made; for a failed request it also keeps the first 2 KB of the gateway's answer, which can quote the request. It never holds the conversation itself. Values from environment variables appear as "not shown", and are replaced with `[env]` if the gateway's answer quotes them.
- The channel list comes from dsh's own channel list and s

dsh-request-params README · The rules file：The page reads and writes `<profile>/.dsh-request-params/config.json`. You can also edit it by hand: the next model request uses the new rules, and an open page loads them within a few seconds (or, if it has unsaved edits, asks what to do).

```json
{
  "version": 1,
  "revision": 3,
  "enabled": true,

dsh-request-params README · The rules file：- `revision` counts saves. A page that saves over a newer revision is stopped and asked what to do.
- A rule may also carry `note` (free text) and `preset` (`{ "id", "form" }`, the form the page reopens). A `preset` that no longer builds exactly this rule's `body` and `headers` is dropped, and the rule stays as a custom rule.
- Fields the page does not know, and values of the wrong type, are dropped when the file is read. A file that is not valid JSON is reported on the page and left untouched; **Move it aside and start fresh** renames it.
- `protocols` holds what you set each endpoint reads, keyed by host and base path: `format` (`openai`, `anthropic`, or `other`) and `extensions` (`openrouter`, `vllm`, `openai`, `helicone`, `cloudflare`), each true or false; false removes one that was detected. Only the page reads it.
- **Export** writes the same object without `revision`. **Import** accepts that object or a bare array of rules; on **Add to current parameters**, an imported protocol replaces yours for the same endpoint.

dsh-request-params README · How it works：dsh's model adapters send requests through the global `fetch`. This plugin wraps `fetch` once. For a POST request with a JSON body that looks like a model call (or that a rule names), it reads the body, applies the matching rules, and sends the changed request; every other request passes through untouched. Responses and streams are never read or changed (only the status, and a failed response's first 2 KB, are noted for the log). Uninstalling the plugin or pausing it puts everything back to what dsh sends by itself.

dsh-request-params README · When a parameter does not seem to apply：1. Open the channel. **Added when sending** shows what its parameters add for the model in the **Model** box. If it says no parameter applies to this model, check the parameter's model scope (the **All models** button).
2. Look at the channel's **Recent requests**, or the **Request log**. If the request is not there, the model request did not go through `fetch` (or no message has been sent since the last restart).
3. Open the request. **No parameters** means the host, model, or path differs from every parameter. A host without a port matches any port; write `127.0.0.1:8130` to match one.
4. **Nothing to change** means the request already had those values.
5. A note that a parameter *has problems* or *uses an environment variable that is not set* says what to fix.
6. If the gateway answers 4xx, open the request: the fields that were added are listed with the gateway's own message. **Pause all parameters** shows whether they are the cause. For OpenRouter, "No endpoints found" usually means the providers you allowed do not serve that model; the routing form flags them for the model in the preview.

dsh-request-params README · Compatibility and limits：- Needs dsh with the web client and Node `^22.19.0 || >=24`. Tested with dsh 0.2.1-rc.2.
- Verified against real dsh runs on three kinds of channel: the official DeepSeek endpoint (`/v1/messages`), an OpenAI-compatible `llm-pi-ai` channel (`/chat/completions`), and an Anthropic-compatible `llm-pi-ai` channel (`/v1/messages`).
- Applies to requests sent through the global `fetch`. A provider that captured its own `fetch` earlier would not be seen; the request log shows what the plugin saw.
- A gateway may ignore or reject fields it does not know. OpenRouter ignores unsupported parameters unless `require_parameters` is on.
- Limits: 100 parameters; per parameter, 64 KB of JSON each for the body fields and the defaults, and 40 headers.

dsh-request-params README · Uninstall：```bash
dsh plugin --profile web remove dsh-request-params
```

Requests go back to what dsh sends by itself. The parameters stay in `<profile>/.dsh-request-params/config.json`, so installing again brings them back; delete the folder to clean up.

dsh-request-params README · Updates：- **Check**: when you open the page, the plugin asks the npm registry DSH is configured with (a mirror works) for the latest version of `dsh-request-params`, at most once every 12 hours. The request names only the package. Turn it off with **Check for updates automatically** at the bottom of the page; **Check for updates** there and in the **⋯** menu still works. Development installs (`link:`) are never checked.
- **Upgrade**: a banner at the top shows a newer release with **See what changed** and **Upgrade…**. After you confirm, DSH's own installer downloads that release's tarball from the registry and installs it, with progress and **Cancel install**. The installer restores the profile's files when an install fails or is cancelled, and the banner then shows the installer's message and the command to upgrade by hand. Only the `latest` release is offered, never a prerelease, and the tarball address must be this package's file on the registry that answered.
- **After the upgrade**: depending on the DSH version, the new version takes over at once (this page closes; open it again) or loads when you restart dsh (web: run `dsh web` again; desktop app:
